clue.text: Proposes to swallow first of the pills

indicators.note: one word taking in another, as a mouth swallows food, puts the second inside the first

parts.note: to table a motion is to propose it for discussion

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone suggests gulping down the first of the pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swallow' puts T, the first letter of 'the', inside TABLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tablets are small pressed doses of medicine, the same thing as pills.

clue.text: Stirs at it vigorously during a long time

indicators.note: during places the jumbled letters inside the period of time

parts.note: ages means a long time

indicators.note: vigorously suggests the words at it are shaken up

explanation.surface: Someone keeps stirring energetically for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vigorously' rearranges AT IT to ITAT, and 'during' puts that inside AGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitating a liquid means shaking or stirring it.

clue.text: Tear delicate fabric — tear badly

parts.note: lace is a fine openwork fabric

indicators.note: badly says the letters of tear are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rips fine lace and makes a mess of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns the second 'tear' into RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to rip or gash flesh, to tear it.

clue.text: Call the servants to book, at first

parts.note: to title is to name or call
pages are young servants

explanation.surface: Summoning servants to be reprimanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to book' looks like reprimanding; the definition is the leaves at the start of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The page bearing a volume's name and author comes first in a printed book.

clue.text: Chop up bones

definitions.meaning: to cut food into small cubes
bones is an old slang term for gaming cubes, once made of bone

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut up some bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting vegetables into cubes is dicing them; and gaming cubes were made of bone, hence the slang.

clue.text: Open prison sufficed

parts.note: can is slang for prison
did, as in 'that did', means sufficed

explanation.surface: An open prison was good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open prison' looks like one phrase; 'Open' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank and honest is being open.

clue.text: Some fried bread for the men, we hear, not getting up

indicators.note: we hear says the word for the men is to be said, not spelt

parts.note: a crew is a group of men working together

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means the word is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Fried bread for the men, apparently, who are not getting out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns CREW into its sound-alike CROU; 'getting up' turns NOT into TON.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a little cube of fried or toasted bread put on soup or salad.

clue.text: Downhill racer supporting exercise as more of a nuisance

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: PE is physical education
a downhill racer goes downhill on skis

explanation.surface: A downhill skier doing workouts becomes increasingly irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts SKIER underneath PE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Peskier is the comparative of pesky, annoying.

clue.text: Said to differ? Acquiesce — or not!

definitions.meaning: to voice a contrary opinion is to state that you differ
acquiesce means go along with; putting a negative on that word gives its opposite

explanation.surface: A puzzled aside about saying yes or no to something.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is playful: take a word for acquiesce, then 'or not' asks you to put its negative prefix DIS- in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To be said to differ is to have stated a contrary view; and adding the negative prefix to a verb of consent gives its opposite.

clue.text: Dangerous creatures found in large two-hulled boats

parts.note: large means big
a catamaran, a boat with two hulls, is called a cat for short

explanation.surface: A warning that something dangerous lurks aboard some big catamarans.
explanation.walkthrough: CATS is short for catamarans, sailing boats with two parallel hulls.
explanation.definitionFit: Lions, tigers and leopards are the big cats, all of them dangerous predators.

clue.text: A hopeless cause — being late, out for nought

parts.note: late can mean deceased, as in 'the late king'
in cricket a batsman out without scoring has made a duck

explanation.surface: A cricketer late to the crease and out without scoring is a lost cause.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a DUCK is a score of zero, from the egg-shaped 0 on the scoreboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead duck is an idiom for a plan or project with no chance of success.

clue.text: Delay union supporting Germany

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means the word sits below the letter for the country

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
an alliance is a union

explanation.surface: Germany is slow to back a union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' places ALLIANCE beneath D in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance can mean dawdling or wasting time, a lingering.

clue.text: Oddly flawed, ruined creature of myth

indicators.note: oddly tells you to take the first, third and fifth letters of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A mythical being described as strangely damaged and spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' takes the odd-numbered letters of 'flawed' (F, A, E) and of 'ruined' (R, I, E).
explanation.definitionFit: Faerie is an old spelling for fairy, a small magical being of folklore.

clue.text: Ponder mail as an anagram for "wet stew", perhaps

indicators.note: as an anagram openly says that the letters of the words before are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Muse on letters that read the same both ways, such as 'wet stew'.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'Ponder mail' are rearranged; 'wet stew' reads the same forwards and backwards, so it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase spelt the same in either direction, like 'wet stew', is the classic example of this kind of wordplay.

clue.text: Niggle over function of seamstress's output

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first word sits above the next

parts.note: to niggle is to needle, to irritate
to function is to work

explanation.surface: Fussing over how a dressmaker's product works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts NEEDLE above WORK in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing and embroidery are what a seamstress produces with her needle.

clue.text: Raise game, though exhausted

definitions.meaning: on a shoot, ... drive birds and animals out of cover so they rise for the guns

explanation.surface: A sportsman lifts his performance even though he is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise game' looks like sporting slang for improving; it is the hunting sense, where beaters flush animals out of hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Beating is driving out quarry for a shoot; and being worn out is colloquially to be dead tired.

clue.text: Gets grime off, leaving sandy deposits in them

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or spoiled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone cleans off dirt but leaves sand behind in the process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals rearranging GETSGRIME; the definition is descriptive, as kitchen hourglasses hold sand that trickles through.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen hourglasses for timing boiled food contain sand that runs from one bulb to the other.

clue.text: Sign that no crop is gathered

indicators.note: gathered suggests the letters are collected up in a new order

explanation.surface: A bad omen: a harvest that has not been brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' rearranges the letters of 'no crop is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio, the scorpion, is a sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Imply that it's private

explanation.surface: Suggest that something is confidential.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something is to suggest it indirectly; and a close, personal matter is a private one.

clue.text: Finishes with victory over king Edward, say!

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: over means turned upside down in a down clue, so the potato word is reversed

parts.note: King Edward is a British potato variety, and spud is slang for potato

explanation.surface: A triumph over King Edward ends things.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato variety, hence SPUD; 'over' turns it to DUPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind-ups are conclusions or endings, as when a meeting winds up.

clue.text: Parliamentary official, one might say

definitions.meaning: the presiding officer of the House of Commons
a person who talks or says things

explanation.surface: A remark about who chairs Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Commons' presiding officer carries this title; and anyone who talks is literally one who utters words.

clue.text: Pine in front of this ice cream

definitions.meaning: put 'pine' before this word and you get the woody fruit of a conifer
a wafer holder for a scoop of ice cream

explanation.surface: A pine tree positioned ahead of an ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a fill-in-the-blank: the answer follows 'pine' to make a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A wafer cornet holding ice cream has the same tapering shape as the seed case of a conifer.

clue.text: Resolve on a simpler objective

indicators.note: resolve can mean break into parts again, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Advice to settle on a more straightforward goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolve' signals rearranging the letters of 'on a simpler'; 'objective' is the adjective meaning detached, not a noun meaning aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Objective and detached both describe a view free of personal feeling.

clue.text: Not often finding artist at bank

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: An artist is seldom found at the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means seldom.

clue.text: Bug, we hear!

parts.note: a bug is an insect, but bugging is also secret listening; the insect's name doubles as a verb for eavesdropping

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that they are being listened in on.
explanation.walkthrough: The insect's name is also a verb meaning to eavesdrop, so 'Bug' and 'we hear' both point to it.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect's name, as a verb, means listening in secretly on others' talk, as a planted bug does.

clue.text: Come back for help before clan's verbal onslaught

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second
come back tells you to read the word for help in the opposite direction

parts.note: help means aid
a clan is a tribe

explanation.surface: Someone returns seeking help ahead of a family's tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come back' turns AID into DIA, which goes before TRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a tirade.

clue.text: Bill opened with request for lounge

indicators.note: opened points to the opening letter of the word bill

parts.note: to request is to ask

explanation.surface: A bill begins with a request to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opened' takes the first letter of 'Bill', which comes before ASK.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge in the sun is to bask, lying idly in warmth.

clue.text: Funny kids' publication, half-hearted

parts.note: a comic is a children's magazine of picture strips

indicators.note: hearted asks for the middle letters, the heart, of the word half

explanation.surface: A children's humour magazine produced without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' is read as the heart of 'half', which is AL, placed after COMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Comical and funny both describe something that makes people laugh.

clue.text: The house of lords in summer is unrivalled

definitions.text: The house of lords in summer
definitions.meaning: in the summer recess the Lords' chamber is empty of its members

explanation.surface: A claim that the upper chamber is at its best in summer.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is Britain's upper chamber of Parliament, whose members are peers; in summer recess it is without them.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a peer, an equal, is to be unmatched.

clue.text: Transgressed, having crossed king, and was fleeced

indicators.note: crossed is read as having a line drawn through, so the king letter sits within the word

parts.note: to transgress is to sin
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A sinner offended the monarch and was robbed as punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having crossed' puts K inside SINNED.
explanation.definitionFit: To skin someone is slang for swindling them out of money, as is to fleece.
